```{r}
sqrt(9)
```
A function takes 1 or more inputs called arguments. They often return an output.

The function is the sqrt(), the input (9) which is the argument and the output is the square root of the number.

```{r}
round(3.14159)
```
```{r}
round(3.14159, digits = 2)
```
This is the rounding function and can be rounded to the required significant figures.

```{r}
print(seq(1,10,2))
print(seq(5,15,5))
```
The sequence function generates a sequence of numbers with the arguments being in order: form (first number). to (last number) and by (the increment).
```{r}
print(seq(by = 2, from = 1, to = 10))
print(seq(by = 5, to = 15, from = 5))
```
The name of the arguments can be used when required.
```{r}
print(rep(2,5))
print(rep(x = 2, times = 5))
```
This function repeats the value,x, for a specific number of times. The order of the arguments is rep(x,times).
```{r}
print(rep(5,7))
print(rep(x = 5, times = 7))
```
